name: Dr. Sournamalya 'Grace' Bhavani
desc: Every great discovery begins as a crazy idea.
title: Computational Astrophysicist & Data Science Fellow
bio: My academic journey began in Electronics and Communication Engineering, where I developed a strong foundation in analytical thinking, problem-solving, and technology. However, during the final stages of my undergraduate studies, I realized that my deepest curiosity lay elsewhere — in understanding the universe and the physical laws that govern it.

This realization motivated me to pursue a new path. To build the theoretical foundation necessary for a career in astrophysics, I enrolled in a Master's degree in Physics while simultaneously studying astronomy, scientific programming, and data analysis independently.

Since then, I have been actively involved in research projects spanning exoplanets, stellar variability, machine learning, and Bayesian statistical methods. These experiences have strengthened my passion for astronomy and reinforced my goal of contributing to astrophysical research through observational data analysis and computational techniques.
Today, I continue to explore the universe through research, collaboration, and lifelong learning, with the long-term goal of bringing the world of Astronomy to everyone.

publications.title: A Unified Bayesian Study of Exoplanet Populations: From Survey Biases to Circumbinary Systems in Kepler and TESS
publications.journal: International Journal of Engineering Research & Technology (IJERT)
publications.authors: Bhavani, S., Sree, D. A., & Premjit, A.
publications.contribution: Data acquisition, preprocessing, Bayesian modeling, posterior predictive checks, WAIC and model comparison.
publications.abstract: A comprehensive Bayesian investigation of exoplanet populations observed by the Kepler and TESS missions. Using hierarchical Bayesian models and statistical inference techniques, the study examined how stellar properties and observational biases influence planetary occurrence and multiplicity across diverse planetary systems.

publications.title: Statistical Approaches to Exoplanet Detection and Characterization Using Photometric Time-Series Data
publications.journal: Frontiers of Cosmology, Astrophysics and Particle Physics (FroCAP2025)
publications.contribution: Explored statistical methods for detecting and characterizing exoplanet signals in photometric datasets, with a focus on time-series analysis and observational uncertainties.
publications.abstract: Explored statistical methodologies for identifying and characterizing exoplanet signatures within photometric datasets. The work focused on time-series analysis, observational uncertainties, and the application of statistical tools to exoplanet detection and characterization.

name: Deepika Sree
desc: Science advances when ideas are shared and explored together.
title: Physics & Machine Learning Researcher
bio: I am a physicist and machine learning researcher with interests at the intersection of physics, machine learning, and scientific computing. My work focuses on developing data-driven and physics-based approaches to solving complex real-world problems by combining tools from machine learning, numerical modeling, and computational physics.

At Star Labs Researches, I contribute to research initiatives that combine physics, astronomy, and computational methods. I am particularly interested in how machine learning and scientific computing can be used to better understand complex systems and address challenging scientific questions.
As part of the Star Labs team, I support collaborative research projects, scientific discussions, and the development of new ideas that bring together curiosity, computation, and discovery.

bio: My interest in astronomy stems from a curiosity about the universe and the physical processes that shape it. As a Master's student in Physics, I am exploring different areas of astrophysics while building a strong foundation in theoretical concepts, scientific research, and data analysis.

Through Star Labs Researches, I have had the opportunity to engage with astronomy research, collaborate with fellow researchers, and gain exposure to modern computational approaches used in astrophysics. These experiences continue to strengthen my interest in understanding the cosmos and contributing to future research efforts.

I am particularly interested in learning how observational data can be used to investigate astronomical phenomena and how computational techniques can help uncover patterns hidden within large scientific datasets.

name: Rajesh M R
desc: Building bridges between science and people through digital storytelling.
title: Digital Media & Science Communication Lead
bio: Rajesh leads the digital media and science communication efforts at Star Labs Researches, ensuring that complex astrophysical research is presented in an engaging and accessible way to the public.
His work bridges the gap between scientific discovery and public understanding, using storytelling, design, and digital platforms to bring the universe closer to everyone.
He collaborates closely with the research team to translate cutting-edge findings into compelling content that inspires curiosity and drives engagement across communities.
